> The operational examples assume that the SSPICE project root is the working directory. They are displayed but not run when the vignette is built because they require project data.

# Why assess correction outcomes?

An algorithm finishing does not imply that every record has been corrected. Step 11 compares original and corrected data, reruns final checks against the extended DAG, and produces a quality report. When available, it also uses the initial check, exact donor records, elapsed time, and donor provenance.

```{r report-step}
source(file.path("scripts", "11_correction_quality_report.R"))
```

The script reads `correction_result.rds` and `corrected_questionnaire_data.rds` from Step 10, as well as `prepared_data_with_logical_edits.rds` and `questionnaire_extended_DAG.rds` from Step 09. It produces `correction_quality_report.rds`, an HTML report, and CSV tables in `correction_quality_output_dir` or the `quality-report` subdirectory of the correction output.

# Interpreting the report

| Question | Evidence to inspect |
|:--|:--|
| How many records were resolved? | Record summary, with unresolved records shown separately |
| Are there remaining violations? | Initial and final reports by record and variable |
| Which values changed? | Change tables and counts by type of change |
| Were the donors eligible? | Provenance and diagnostics for the `EXACT` donor pool |
| Were constrained variables respected? | Audit of immutable variables and exogenous VAUX variables |
| How much time did the process take? | Elapsed time and execution summary |

Assess the resolution rate separately from the persistence of errors. A record may remain unresolved; do not treat it as corrected solely because a value changed. Retain the full output and pilot settings to make the comparison reproducible.
